newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Four youths shot dead ahead of S.Africa peace talkS.
newsitem.headline: Four youths shot dead ahead of S.Africa peace talkS.

text.p: Four youths were shot dead in their home in South Africa's volatile KwaZulu- Natal province on Thursday, a day before Deputy President Thabo Mbeki was due to start a visit to bolster peace.

Violence monitors said on Friday they suspected it was another political attack in the bloody Zulu turf war between supporters of President Nelson Mandela's African National Congress (ANC) and members of Mangosuthu Buthelezi's Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP).
Gunmen wielding AK-47 assault rifles attacked the sleeping family on Thursday night in the Zwalibovu area 20 km (12.5 miles) west of the port city of Durban, a police statement said.
The deceased are aged from 15 to eight.

Jessica McKay of the independent Human Rights Committee said the latest violence -- the third politically related killing since the beginning of the year -- stemmed from rivalry between an ANC councillor and an Inkatha-supporting chief in the area.
"That area has been problematic and we suspect this killing was politically motivated. The place is brewing up and people have vacated the area out of fear," McKay told Reuters.
The murders come as the ANC and Inkatha are holding top-level peace talks to try to stem the political violence that has wracked the province for over a decade and killed some 15,000 people.
Mbeki arrived in KwaZulu-Natal on Friday to meet with the Inkatha-dominated provincial government and traditional chiefs, a large number of whom are aligned to the Zulu-based Inkatha.
Mbeki will meet Buthelezi in Durban on Saturday to discuss the peace process between the two parties, whose rivalry began in 1979 when they disagreed on how best to resist apartheid.
The ANC has suggested a special amnesty deal to fill the gaps left by the Truth and Reconciliation Commission, which is acknowledged to have been unsuccessful in KwaZulu-Natal.
The truth commission, a statutory body probing 30 years of apartheid-era human rights abuses, has been accused by Inkatha of being biased in favour of the ANC.
The ANC has also proposed a more senior position for Buthelezi in government, which top ANC sources say could mean a deputy presidency.
Inkatha insists on more autonomy for the province and increased power for traditional leaders in local government before peace talks can start in earnest.
